note: Place of the day (PRD F-16). One entry per day in this order, starting with the first on 2026-11-14 and switching at midnight Berlin time. Texts are our own words; images come from Wikimedia Commons with their licence.

places.name: Eiffel Tower
places.text: Built as the entrance arch for the 1889 World's Fair, Gustave Eiffel's iron tower was the tallest structure in the world for four decades.

places.name: Machu Picchu
places.text: A 15th-century Inca citadel on a mountain ridge high above the Urubamba valley.

places.name: Taj Mahal
places.text: A white marble mausoleum that the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan had built for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

places.name: Niagara Falls
places.text: Three waterfalls on the border between Canada and the United States, where the Niagara River drops on its way from Lake Erie to Lake Ontario.

places.name: Uluru
places.text: A huge sandstone monolith in the heart of Australia, sacred to the Anangu people.

places.name: Brandenburg Gate
places.text: Berlin's neoclassical gate from the 1790s stood in the no-man's-land of the Wall for almost three decades and became a symbol of reunification.

places.name: Victoria Falls
places.text: The Zambezi plunges into a narrow gorge here. Locally the falls are called Mosi-oa-Tunya, the smoke that thunders.

places.name: Mount Fuji
places.text: Japan's highest mountain is an active volcano that last erupted in 1707.

places.name: Grand Canyon
places.text: The Colorado River has carved this canyon, in places more than 1.8 km deep.

places.name: Colosseum
places.text: Ancient Rome's largest amphitheatre, completed in 80 AD, once held tens of thousands of spectators.

places.name: Christ the Redeemer
places.text: The Art Deco statue of Jesus has looked out over Rio de Janeiro from the summit of Corcovado since 1931.

places.name: Petra
places.text: A city carved into rose-coloured rock, once the capital of the Nabataean kingdom.

places.name: Sydney Opera House
places.text: Jørn Utzon's shell-roofed performing arts centre on Sydney Harbour opened in 1973.

places.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
places.text: King Ludwig II of Bavaria's 19th-century fairy-tale castle above the Pöllat gorge.

places.name: Pyramids of Giza
places.text: The Great Pyramid is the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World and the only one still largely intact.

places.name: Iguazu Falls
places.text: Hundreds of waterfalls along the border of Argentina and Brazil.

places.name: Great Wall of China
places.text: A system of walls and watchtowers built and rebuilt over many centuries across northern China.

places.name: Statue of Liberty
places.text: A gift from France to the United States, dedicated in 1886 at the entrance to New York Harbor.

places.name: Santorini
places.text: White villages line the rim of a flooded caldera left by one of the largest volcanic eruptions in human history.

places.name: Angkor Wat
places.text: Built in the 12th century, it is one of the largest religious monuments in the world.

places.name: Table Mountain
places.text: The flat-topped mountain rises above Cape Town.

places.name: Sagrada Família
places.text: Antoni Gaudí's basilica in Barcelona has been under construction since 1882.

places.name: Golden Gate Bridge
places.text: The suspension bridge across the Golden Gate strait opened in 1937.

places.name: Ha Long Bay
places.text: Thousands of limestone islands and islets rise from the Gulf of Tonkin.

places.name: Stonehenge
places.text: A prehistoric ring of standing stones on Salisbury Plain, raised in stages from around 3000 BC.

places.name: Mount Kilimanjaro
places.text: Africa's highest mountain is a dormant volcano.

places.name: Chichen Itza
places.text: A large Maya city on the Yucatán Peninsula, crowned by the stepped pyramid El Castillo.

places.name: Burj Khalifa
places.text: At 828 m, the Dubai skyscraper has been the tallest building in the world since 2010.

places.name: Matterhorn
places.text: The pyramid-shaped peak on the Swiss–Italian border was first climbed in 1865.

places.name: Galápagos Islands
places.text: Volcanic islands in the Pacific whose unique wildlife helped Charles Darwin develop his theory of evolution.

places.name: Hagia Sophia
places.text: Built as a cathedral in 537, the Istanbul landmark has also served as a mosque and a museum.

places.name: Moraine Lake
places.text: A glacier-fed lake in the Canadian Rockies, famous for its turquoise water.

places.name: Forbidden City
places.text: The imperial palace of the Ming and Qing dynasties in the heart of Beijing.

places.name: Mont-Saint-Michel
places.text: A tidal island crowned by a medieval abbey.

places.name: Salar de Uyuni
places.text: The world's largest salt flat, high in the Bolivian Andes.

places.name: Great Barrier Reef
places.text: The world's largest coral reef system stretches along the coast of Queensland.

places.name: Acropolis of Athens
places.text: The rocky hill above Athens carries the Parthenon, a temple to the goddess Athena completed in the 5th century BC.

places.name: Grand Prismatic Spring
places.text: The largest hot spring in the United States is ringed by bands of colour from heat-loving microbes.

places.name: Borobudur
places.text: A 9th-century temple on Java and the largest Buddhist monument in the world.

places.name: Alhambra
places.text: A palace and fortress complex of the Nasrid dynasty above Granada.

places.name: Lake Baikal
places.text: The deepest and oldest freshwater lake on Earth.

places.name: Monument Valley
places.text: Sandstone buttes rise from the desert on the Navajo Nation.

places.name: Cologne Cathedral
places.text: Begun in 1248 and completed in 1880, Germany's best-known Gothic cathedral.

places.name: Sossusvlei
places.text: A salt and clay pan surrounded by some of the highest red sand dunes in the world.

places.name: Fushimi Inari-taisha
places.text: Thousands of vermilion torii gates line the paths up the sacred mountain of this shrine.

places.name: Teotihuacan
places.text: An ancient city with the Pyramid of the Sun, one of the largest pyramids in the Americas.

places.name: Venice
places.text: A city built on more than a hundred small islands in a lagoon, linked by canals and bridges.

places.name: Perito Moreno Glacier
places.text: A huge glacier in Patagonia that ends in a wall of ice on Lake Argentino.

places.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
places.text: The white marble mosque has room for more than 40,000 worshippers.

places.name: Geirangerfjord
places.text: A narrow fjord framed by steep mountains and waterfalls.

places.name: Bagan
places.text: Thousands of Buddhist temples and pagodas cover the plain of this ancient royal city.

places.name: Mount Rushmore
places.text: The faces of four US presidents are carved into the granite of the Black Hills.

places.name: Pamukkale
places.text: White travertine terraces filled with warm spring water.

places.name: Saint Basil's Cathedral
places.text: The colourful onion domes of this 16th-century church stand on Red Square.

places.name: Jökulsárlón
places.text: Icebergs from the Breiðamerkurjökull glacier drift through this lagoon towards the sea.

places.name: Petronas Towers
places.text: The twin skyscrapers were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004.

places.name: Cliffs of Moher
places.text: Sea cliffs on Ireland's west coast that rise more than 200 m above the Atlantic.

places.name: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park
places.text: Thousands of sandstone pillars rise from the forests of Hunan.

places.name: Tre Cime di Lavaredo
places.text: Three distinctive rock towers in the Dolomites.

places.name: Wadi Rum
places.text: A desert valley of sandstone and granite mountains in southern Jordan.

places.name: Hallstatt
places.text: A village on the shore of the Hallstätter See, home to one of the oldest salt mines in the world.

places.name: Tower Bridge
places.text: The bascule and suspension bridge over the Thames opened in 1894.

places.name: Sparrenburg
places.text: The castle above Bielefeld dates back to the 13th century.
